claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a son, Alex. He's 21 years old and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. 

Since Alex is 21 years old, I need to understand a bit more about his situation, as Child Benefit generally has age-related criteria.

Is Alex currently in full-time, non-advanced education or on an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Just to make sure I have all the information needed, is Alex registered with the official careers service (or equivalent service in your area), or does he have any other circumstances that might be relevant, such as a disability or health condition?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not registered with any careers service and there aren't any health conditions or disabilities to mention.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

Just one final question to ensure I have a complete picture: Are you the person responsible for Alex - meaning do you live with him and are you responsible for his care and upbringing?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me. I do help him out financially though - I give him about £20 a week for things he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

Based on what you've told me, I'm afraid Alex would not be eligible for Child Benefit. Here's why:

Child Benefit is generally only payable for children under 16, or under 20 if they're in approved full-time non-advanced education or training. Since Alex is 21 years old and not in education or approved training, he falls outside the age eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

Additionally, even if he were within the age range, you would typically need to be responsible for him - which usually means he would need to be living with you.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about Child Benefit eligibility?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, that's clear. Thank you for explaining it to me. I understand now that because Alex is over 20 and not in education or training, I can't claim Child Benefit for him. I appreciate your help.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify the situation for you. I understand it may be disappointing, but I hope the explanation was helpful in understanding why Alex doesn't qualify in this case.

If your circumstances change in the future, or if you have any other questions about benefits, feel free to reach out. Take care!
